### Observed differences

- The two alternative entry routes swapped shares. In the earlier window, A01, A05, A07 and A09 each appeared in about 46 in 100 traces, while A03, A11, A12 and A13 each appeared in about 55 in 100; in the later window the first group rose to about 53–54 in 100 and the second fell to about 47–48 in 100 — a shift of roughly 7–8 traces in 100. All eight activities remain well observed in each window (about 91–110 supporting traces), none becomes noticeably more repetitive, and the two groups' shares sum to about one per trace in both windows, consistent with every trace taking exactly one of the two routes. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]

- The two groups form two blocks that converge on the same continuation. A01 is followed by A05, A07 or A09 (roughly 23–40 in 100 of A01's outgoing transitions each), these three follow one another in flexible order and then hand over to A14; A03 is followed by A11, A12 or A13, which likewise precede A14, and A14 itself runs in every trace in both windows. Handovers to A14 inside the blocks shifted only a little (for example A07 passed to A14 in about 42 in 100 of its transitions before and 31 after, while A09 passed to A14 in about 29 before and 38 after). [DIR001, DIR003, DIR005, DIR007, DIR009, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, OCC014]

- Further into the process, the split after A46 moved toward A47: about 44 in 100 of A46's outgoing transitions went to A47 in the earlier window and about 51 in the later, while transitions to A48 fell from about 54 to 46. A47 then ran in more traces (about 61 vs 67 in 100) and repeated more often (average 0.77 vs 0.91 occurrences per trace), whereas A48 and A49 kept a similar trace presence (about 61–63 in 100) but were repeated less (averages 0.94 vs 0.84 and 0.95 vs 0.83; traces with repeats down from about 21 to 15 in 100). [DIR046, OCC041, OCC042, OCC043]

- The side loop through A43 was used more: A43 appeared in about 14 in 100 traces before and about 21 after, A44's average occurrences rose from 0.71 to 0.81 per trace (repeats in about 14 vs 21 in 100 traces), and A44 returned to A43 more often (about 33 vs 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) while continuing to A45 less often (about 66 vs 58). [OCC038, OCC039, DIR044]

- Smaller shifts: A19 rose from about 31 to 38 in 100 traces while A25 fell from 36 to 32 (both lead on to A26); A23 fell from about 52 to 44 in 100 and A24 rose from about 50 to 56; A10 rose from about 21 to 26; and A15 and A16, present in every trace, repeated slightly more often (repeats in about 35 vs 41–42 in 100 traces). [OCC019, OCC025, OCC023, OCC024, OCC010, OCC015, OCC016, DIR019, DIR025]

- Activities on the shared spine (A14, A27, A28, A29, A33, A34, A35, A37, A38, A46, A50) ran in every trace in both windows with occurrence averages changing by at most about 0.03, so the shifts above are localised rather than global. [OCC014, OCC026, OCC027, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, OCC031, OCC032, OCC033, OCC040, OCC044]

- Several of the largest direction-profile differences — at A02, A06, A08 and A51 — rest on few observed outgoing transitions (about 33–46 before and 32–38 after; A51 only 4 versus 11) and are too weak to interpret on their own. [DIR002, DIR006, DIR008, DIR051]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two existing alternative routes were taken with different frequencies: in the later window, the route entering through A01 and continuing through A05, A07 and A09 was executed in about 53–54 in 100 traces (up from about 46), while the alternative route through A03, A11, A12 and A13 fell to about 47–48 in 100 (from about 55). The support is direct and consistent: the participation of exactly these eight activities moved in two lockstep groups of four with matching shift sizes and opposite directions; the groups' shares sum to about one per trace in both windows, so the difference reads as whole traces being rerouted between the blocks rather than as activities becoming optional, repeated or bypassed; the flexible order inside each block and the convergence on A14 are preserved; and the directly-follows profiles confirm the block structure. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is a coincidental alignment of the two finite samples — the screening summary that would show how many qualifying items an unchanged process typically produces is not part of this evidence — although each of the eight differences is larger than in roughly 62–87 of 100 random re-splits. The choice point between the two routes is itself not observed, so the alternative-routes reading rests on the complementary participation pattern. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR001, DIR003, DIR005, DIR007, DIR009, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, OCC014]

Other differences:
- A second, independent-looking shift in path frequencies occurred after A46: the split moved toward A47 (about 44 to 51 in 100 of A46's outgoing transitions, with A48 down from about 54 to 46), after which A47 ran and repeated more often (average 0.77 to 0.91 per trace) while A48 and A49 repeated less (averages 0.94 to 0.84 and 0.95 to 0.83); the evidence shows no connection between this shift and the entry-route shift. [DIR046, OCC041, OCC042, OCC043]
- The A43 side loop ran more often (A43 in about 14 vs 21 in 100 traces; A44 average occurrences 0.71 to 0.81; A44 returning to A43 in about 33 vs 40 in 100 of its transitions instead of continuing to A45). [OCC038, OCC039, DIR044]
- Small participation shifts at A19 (about 31 to 38 in 100) with A25 down (36 to 32), at A23 (52 to 44) and A24 (50 to 56), at A10 (21 to 26), and slightly more repetition of A15 and A16. [OCC019, OCC025, OCC023, OCC024, OCC010, OCC015, OCC016]
